q: Which describes good practice when drawing a mitochondrion for an IB exam?
options: Shade the cristae and matrix to show depth, and put arrowheads on the ends of the label lines
Draw both membranes as a single line, which keeps the diagram simple, clear and quick to label
Clear unbroken lines, no shading, ruled label lines that don't cross, and both membranes shown
Write each label directly on top of the structure it names, so no label lines are needed at all
explanation: Drawing marks are awarded for clear, correctly labelled structures. Use sharp continuous lines with no shading; show the envelope as two separate lines with the inner membrane folded into cristae; draw label lines with a ruler, without arrowheads, ending exactly on the structure and never crossing; print labels neatly to the side. Add a title and, where relevant, a scale bar or magnification.
